questions.question: In a periodic-review single-item inventory system with backlogging, which expression gives the inventory position at the start of a period? (Stock on order means units ordered but not yet received.)
options: On-hand stock plus backlogged demand plus stock on order
On-hand stock plus stock on order
On-hand stock minus backlogged demand plus stock on order
On-hand stock minus backlogged demand

questions.question: In a periodic-review inventory system with lead time $l\ge1$ periods, an order of size $Q_k>0$ is placed at the start of period $k$ and arrives at the start of period $k+l$. How do the inventory position $P$ and the inventory level $I$ respond when the order is placed?
options: $P$ rises by $Q_k$ at once; $I$ stays unchanged until period $k+l$
$P$ and $I$ both rise by $Q_k$ at once, at the start of period $k$
$I$ rises by $Q_k$ at once; $P$ rises only when the units arrive
Neither changes yet; both rise by $Q_k$ at the start of period $k+l$

questions.question: A periodic-review inventory system has lead time $l=0$, so an order placed at the start of period $k$ arrives immediately, and it starts with $P_1=I_1$ and nothing on order. Which relation between the position $P_k$ and the level $I_k$ holds for every $k\ge1$, whatever demands occur and whatever orders $Q_k\ge0$ are placed?
options: $P_k=I_k+Q_k$, with $Q_k$ the order placed in period $k$
$P_k=I_k$, because no order is ever outstanding
$P_k=I_k+Q_{k-1}$, the order placed one period earlier
$P_k=I_k^+$, the on-hand stock without any backlog

questions.question: In a periodic-review inventory system with backlogging, lead time $l\ge1$, orders $Q_k\ge0$, and $P_1=I_1$ with nothing on order initially, which inequality involving the position $P_k$, the level $I_k$ or the on-hand stock $I_k^+$ holds in every period, for every demand and order sequence?
options: $P_k\le I_k$, because received units leave the order pipeline
$P_k\ge0$, because a position counts stock and open orders
$P_k\ge I_k^+$, because orders can only add to on-hand stock
$P_k\ge I_k$, because the quantity on order is never negative

questions.question: Base-stock, $(s,S)$, $(Q,r)$ and $(T,S)$ policies with lead time $l\ge1$ decide each order from the inventory position rather than from the inventory level. What is the reason?
options: The position is never negative, so order sizes stay non-negative
The level ignores backlogged demand, whereas the position includes it
The level sees an order only on arrival, so a rule on it reorders units on the way
The position equals the on-hand stock at the moment the new order arrives

questions.question: A $(Q,r)$ policy with $Q=5$ and $r=3$ orders, at the start of period $k$, the smallest number of lots of $5$ that brings the position into $\{4,\dots,8\}$ whenever $P_{k-1}'\le3$, and nothing otherwise; the lead time is $l=1$. At the end of period $k-1$ the position is $P_{k-1}'=-4$ and the level is $I_{k-1}'=-8$. What is the position $P_k$ after the order?

In a periodic-review inventory system with lead time $l=2$, the position at the start of period $k-1$ is $P_{k-1}=10$, demand in period $k-1$ is $D_{k-1}=3$, and an order $Q_k=5$ is placed at the start of period $k$. What is the position $P_k$?

An $(s,S)$ policy with $s=3$ and $S=10$ orders $S-P_{k-1}'$ at the start of period $k$ if the end-of-period position satisfies $P_{k-1}'\le s$, and nothing otherwise. The lead time is $l=2$; at the end of period $k-1$, $P_{k-1}'=4$ and the level is $I_{k-1}'=1$. How much is ordered?
options: $0$ units
$9$ units
$6$ units
$7$ units

questions.question: At the end of period $k-1$ an inventory system has position $P_{k-1}'=9$ and level $I_{k-1}'=2$, with one outstanding order of $7$ units. That order arrives at the start of period $k$, and no new order is placed then, so $Q_k=0$. What are the position $P_k$ and the level $I_k$?
options: Position $16$, level $9$
Position $9$, level $2$
Position $9$, level $9$
Position $16$, level $2$

questions.question: A periodic-review inventory system has lead time $l=1$, with $P_1=I_1$ and nothing on order initially. At the start of period $k$, the order $Q_{k-1}=4$ placed one period earlier has just arrived, giving level $I_k=2$, and a new order $Q_k=5$ is placed. What is the position $P_k$?

Two copies of one periodic-review inventory system face identical demands $D_1,D_2,\dots$, start from $P_1=I_1$ with nothing on order, and follow the same $(s,S)$ policy on the end-of-period position. One has lead time $l=0$, the other $l=3$. How do their paths compare?
options: Positions $P_k$ coincide in every period; only the levels $I_k$ differ
The levels agree throughout, and the lead time alters only the positions
The $l=3$ positions are the $l=0$ positions delayed by three periods
Positions and levels coincide, since both systems face the same demand

questions.question: In a periodic-review inventory system with backlogging and order sizes $Q_k\ge0$, the inventory position at the start of a period is $P_k=-4$. Which statement about the system at that moment must be true?
options: Exactly $4$ units are backlogged and nothing is on order
The backlog exceeds the quantity on order by exactly $4$ units
An order of $4$ units has been placed but not yet received
On-hand stock is $4$ units and an equal amount is backlogged

questions.question: An $(s,S)$ policy with $s<S$ and lead time $l\ge1$ orders $S-P_{k-1}'$ at the start of period $k$ whenever $P_{k-1}'\le s$, starting from $P_1=I_1=S$. Which statement about the start-of-period position $P_k$ (after any order) and the level $I_k$ holds in every period, for every demand sequence?
options: $P_k=S$ always, since every period starts with an order up to $S$
The level stays within $s<I_k\le S$, whereas the position can drop below $s$
Both $P_k$ and $I_k$ lie in the closed interval from $s$ to $S$
$s<P_k\le S$ always, whereas the level can drop below $s$ or below zero

questions.question: An inventory system with lead time $l=2$ ends period $k-1$ with position $P_{k-1}'=6$ and level $I_{k-1}'=-1$. The intended rule is to order up to $S=12$ if the end-of-period position is at most $s=4$, but the rule is mistakenly applied to the level. What does the position $P_k$ become after the mistaken order?

In a periodic-review system with lead time $l=2$, $P_1=I_1$ and nothing on order initially, the start of period $k$ shows position $P_k=9$ and level $I_k=-3$, and the order placed at the start of period $k$ is $Q_k=5$. What was the order $Q_{k-1}$?

An $(s,S)=(2,8)$ policy orders $8-P_{k-1}'$ at the start of period $k$ when $P_{k-1}'\le2$. The lead time is $l=2$, $P_1=I_1=8$ with nothing on order, and demands are $D_1=3$, $D_2=4$, $D_3=1$. What are the position $P_4$ and the level $I_4$?
options: Position $7$, level $7$
Position $7$, level $0$
Position $15$, level $0$
Position $8$, level $1$

questions.question: With lead time $l=2$ a system runs $P_k=P_{k-1}'+Q_k$ and $I_k=I_{k-1}'+Q_{k-2}$. At the start of period $1$, $I_1=4$ and $Q_1=0$, but an order $Q_0=6$ placed at the start of period $0$ is still on its way and arrives at the start of period $2$. The position is nevertheless initialised as $P_1=I_1=4$, forgetting this order. For $k\ge1$, how does $P_k-I_k$ compare with the true quantity on order?
options: It is $6$ units too small in period $1$ only; from period $2$, when $Q_0$ arrives, the two agree
It is $6$ units too small in periods $1$ and $2$ and correct from period $3$ on, after one lead time
It is $6$ units too large in every period, because the forgotten order is missing from the level
It is $6$ units too small in every period, however many orders are placed later

questions.question: A periodic-review system with lead time $l=3$ and orders $Q_k\ge0$ starts with $P_1=I_1$ and nothing on order. At the start of some period $k\ge4$, the position equals the level, $P_k=I_k$. What can be concluded?
options: No order was placed in periods $k-2$, $k-1$ and $k$
The orders of the three periods before period $k$ were all zero
There is no backlog at the start of period $k$
The lead time must effectively be zero in that period

questions.question: Deterministic demand runs at $D=10$ units per day, the EOQ batch $y^*=50$ gives a cycle of $t_0^*=5$ days, and the lead time is $L=12$ days, so on-hand stock triggers an order at $DL_e=20$, with $L_e=L-\lfloor L/t_0^*\rfloor t_0^*$. Without backlog, what is the inventory position just before each order is placed?
options: $20$ units
$120$ units
$70$ units
$170$ units

questions.question: A base-stock policy with level $S=10$ orders $Q_k=S-P_{k-1}'$ at the start of every period, starting from $P_1=I_1=S$ with nothing on order, so $Q_k=D_{k-1}$. The lead time is $l=2$. In periods $k-3$, $k-2$, $k-1$ (with $k\ge5$) the demands are $3$, $3$ and $4$. What is the level $I_k$?
